one_liner: Enterprise cloud CRM platform for sales, service, marketing and custom apps.
auth_notes: Every API call needs auth via a supported OAuth flow or a SOAP login() session ID (Trailhead). Spring '26 restricts creation of new Connected Apps by default (UI and Metadata API, except via package install); re-enabling needs Salesforce Support, and External Client Apps (ECAs) are recommended. ECAs support only modern OAuth flows (no username/password) and do not exist in a target org until installed. Hosted MCP uses OAuth via ECAs only (scopes mcp_api, refresh_token).
access_notes: API is available on Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Performance and Professional (with add-on) editions; user needs the 'API Enabled' permission. Sales Cloud pricing lists 'Web Services API' as an extra $25/user/month on Pro Suite. Developer Edition (free signup) has API access, but developer.salesforce.com returned 403 so the 'free' claim was not confirmed on a fetched page.
api_breadth_notes: REST, SOAP, Bulk, Pub/Sub (gRPC), Connect REST, UI API, Analytics REST, Metadata, Tooling, Apex REST/SOAP and GraphQL; generic sObject CRUD/query over hundreds of standard objects.
mcp_notes: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers (GA per forcedotcom/mcp-hosted repo). Remote base URL https://api.salesforce.com/platform/mcp/v1/ with path per org type, e.g. d/{mydomain}/{servername}. Needs Enterprise Edition or higher, and Developer Edition is supported. Servers are disabled by default and enabled under Setup > API Catalog > MCP Servers. Tool calls count against the org's daily API quota. OAuth via External Client App.
blocker: New OAuth apps must be External Client Apps, installed per org
notes: developer.salesforce.com returned HTTP 403 for every fetch (REST guide, editions page, hosted MCP guide), so evidence comes from Trailhead, the salesforce.com blog and pricing pages, and the official forcedotcom GitHub wiki. 'Webhooks' means event-driven integration (Pub/Sub API, Platform Events/CDC, outbound messages) rather than generic webhooks. Sandboxes and scratch orgs exist; the MCP wiki documents their URL patterns. A multi-org OAuth toolkit needs to account for the ECA shift: ECAs are local to an org until installed or packaged, so verify the distribution path (packaged ECA) before launch. Search snippets mention Flex Credits billing for hosted MCP, but no fetched page confirmed it.

one_liner: CRM platform with marketing, sales, service, content and operations hubs.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 is required to distribute to multiple accounts (marketplace or allowlisted). A static auth access token covers a single account (the legacy private app pattern). The developer API key (hapikey) is only for some app-management endpoints, not general data calls. Tokens are sent as Bearer.
access_notes: Free CRM accounts get API limits (Free/Starter: 100 req/10s per app, 250k/day). Developer test accounts are free (up to 10, with a 90-day trial of many Enterprise features). Distribution is gated: static-token apps work in 1 account, private OAuth apps in up to 10 allowlisted accounts, and marketplace OAuth apps in up to 25 accounts until HubSpot Ecosystem Quality review and Marketplace listing, after which installs are unlimited.
api_breadth_notes: Many product areas: CRM objects and associations, engagements, marketing, CMS, conversations, automation, webhooks and more; date-versioned APIs (e.g. /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts). Easily 100+ operations.
mcp_notes: Remote HubSpot MCP server at https://mcp.hubspot.com. OAuth with PKCE via an MCP connector (Development > MCP Connectors), with user-level permissions and read/write across CRM records, activities, content, campaigns and more. Some tools are BETA (revenue objects, quotes) or plan-gated (AEO, quotes). There is also a local Developer MCP server via the HubSpot CLI (hs mcp setup).
blocker: Unlisted OAuth app capped at 25 installs until Marketplace review
notes: Build and test fully for free with developer test accounts (https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/getting-started/account-types). A multi-tenant OAuth toolkit needs Marketplace listing review to pass 25 installs. Marketplace-distributed apps are rate-limited to 110 req/10s per installing account. The webhooks subscription API works with legacy public apps; project-based (2025.2+) apps configure webhooks in config or use the journal APIs (https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/webhooks/guide). Legacy developer accounts were migrated to standard accounts on March 9, 2026.

one_liner: Pipeline-focused sales CRM for small and mid-size sales teams.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 is for apps (client_id/secret from Developer Hub). The personal API token goes in the x-api-token header; it is tied to one user and company, only one is active at a time, and regenerating it breaks existing integrations.
access_notes: Developer sandbox account is requested via a form on the developer site. It is like a regular company account with Developer Hub access, limited to 5 seats, and deleted if inactive (no app in 45 days, or none live in 6 months). The fetched docs and Developer Agreement do not state a price, and Pipedrive may refuse sandbox signups at its discretion. Private apps can be shared with any company via an unlisted install link without Marketplace review; public Marketplace listing needs Pipedrive approval.
api_breadth_notes: 48 endpoint groups in the v1 reference (deals, persons, organizations, leads, activities, products, pipelines, projects, users/roles, webhooks, etc.); v2 OpenAPI spec also exists.
mcp_notes: Native hosted MCP server launched June 30, 2026: OAuth connection, available on all Pipedrive plans, read/write (deals, contacts, orgs, leads, activities). Listed in Claude's connector directory. Search results give the URL https://mcp.pipedrive.ai/mcp, but no fetched page confirmed it.
notes: No free plan (pricing page returned 403). The sandbox is the free dev path, but its $0 cost is implied, not stated. OAuth app distribution without review works via private app install links (https://pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-registering-a-private-app). Prefer API v2 endpoints where available. MCP usage counts against plan token limits per search results (not verified on a fetched page).

one_liner: Flexible, data-driven CRM with customizable objects, lists and workflows.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 auth-code flow for multi-workspace apps; per-workspace API keys generated in the developer console. Bearer header, with HTTP Basic (token as username) also accepted. Scopes are per token. Workspace-level tokens are the default (admin grant); user-level tokens are OAuth-only and need PKCE. Webhook endpoints accept workspace tokens only.
access_notes: Free plan ($0, up to 3 users) appears to include 'API and webhooks', 'App SDK' and 'MCP server' (pricing page text lacked checkmarks). New workspaces get a 14-day Pro trial. SQL via API/MCP is Ultra-only. Unpublished OAuth apps can be installed in up to 25 workspaces before Attio approval.
api_breadth_notes: About 160 endpoint pages: objects, attributes, records, lists/entries, notes, tasks, comments/threads, meetings, call recordings, files, webhooks, workspace members, SCIM, SQL.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp, OAuth with Attio login (no API key), about 53 tools (records, lists, notes, tasks, meetings, emails, reporting, read-only SQL). Read tools are auto-approved and write tools need confirmation. kesslerio/attio-mcp-server is community-built.
blocker: Unpublished OAuth app limited to 25 workspaces until approval
notes: Easy to build and test on the Free plan. Public OpenAPI spec at https://api.attio.com/openapi/api (linked from docs, not fetched). The 25-workspace cap only matters for broad OAuth distribution; per-workspace API keys work without approval. Developer console is build.attio.com.

one_liner: Open-source CRM, self-hostable or cloud, with REST/GraphQL APIs and app SDK.
auth_notes: API keys are created under Settings > Developers > API, shown once, sent as Bearer, and can be limited to a role. OAuth is for external apps acting on behalf of users (separate OAuth docs, not fetched). The MCP server supports OAuth with automatic client registration, or an API key.
access_notes: Open-source core is free to self-host (Docker Compose), giving $0 credentials. Twenty Cloud has no free plan: 30-day trial without a credit card, then Pro $9, Organization $39/user/month, Enterprise from $50k/yr. API and webhooks are included on all Cloud plans (50/100 calls per min on Pro/Org).
api_breadth_notes: Schema-generated per workspace: Core API (CRUD/filter/relations for every standard and custom object) plus Metadata API (objects, fields, relations), in both REST and GraphQL. Generic surface rather than many distinct product areas.
mcp_notes: Built-in MCP endpoint at {workspace URL}/mcp (e.g. mycompany.twenty.com/mcp on Cloud, own domain when self-hosted). Streamable HTTP, OAuth (recommended) or API key. Record, metadata, workflow, dashboard, view, webhook and other tools; modes default, direct and meta.
notes: Base URL varies: Cloud https://api.twenty.com/, self-hosted https://{domain}/, so the toolkit should take the base URL as a connection field. There is no static API reference; endpoints are generated from each workspace's schema (custom objects included), so tools should discover objects through the metadata API. Batch up to 60 records per call; docs state 100 req/min. 'access' is self_serve_free only through self-hosting; Cloud testing beyond 30 days needs a paid plan.

one_liner: Customizable work-management platform with no-code apps, workspaces and workflows.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 with server-side, client-side, username/password and app-authentication flows. Self-registered client ID/secret from the API key page. Header is 'Authorization: OAuth2 <token>'. Access tokens last 8h and refresh tokens 28 days.
access_notes: Free plan ($0, up to 5 users, 100 items per org) includes 1,000 API calls/hour, the same base limit as Plus and Premium; paid API add-ons raise it to 2,500-50,000/hr. 30-day Premium trial for eligible free orgs.
api_breadth_notes: 43 API areas (9 core: applications, items, tasks, comments, contacts, files, hooks, OAuth, status; plus spaces, orgs, search, stream, views, flows, etc.).
mcp_notes: Official Podio MCP Server (Progress) at https://mcp.podio.com/mcp, hosted remote. OAuth (authorize/token at mcp.podio.com), with shared default credentials for testing (about 30-40 requests) or your own Podio API key for production. 22 read/write tools. Marked beta.
notes: Podio is now under Progress (docs and pricing on progress.com). The free plan's 100-item cap limits realistic test data. The 1,000 calls/hour limit is low for agent workloads. Webhooks are 'Hooks' that call external URLs on Podio events. The username/password flow should be avoided.

one_liner: Cloud CRM for sales automation, pipeline management and customer engagement.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 auth-code flow with client ID/secret from a registered client. Access tokens last about 1h; refresh tokens last until revoked. Scoped tokens. Multi-DC: start auth at accounts.zoho.com (US/EU/AU/IN) or accounts.zoho.com.cn, then use the returned location/accounts-server to pick the API domain (zohoapis.com, .eu, .in, .com.au, .jp, .com.cn, zohocloud.ca). Enable Multi-DC per client in the API console.
access_notes: API credit limits cover the Free edition (5,000 credits/day, concurrency 5); paid editions get 50k base plus per-license credits. Trials have the same limits as their paid edition.
api_breadth_notes: v8 groups: Metadata, Core (records), Composite, Bulk, Notification and Query (COQL) APIs across all CRM modules, including custom modules.
mcp_notes: Zoho-hosted Zoho CRM MCP servers (4 prebuilt: Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, Workflow & Process Automation), OAuth via Zoho login with role-based permissions. Calls count against API credits. Endpoint and GA/beta status are not stated on the fetched page. Zoho also runs a broader Zoho MCP platform (not fetched).
notes: The toolkit must handle multi-data-center domains (https://www.zoho.com/crm/developer/docs/api/v8/multi-dc.html). Free-edition API access is inferred from the credit table listing a Free tier rather than stated outright. The Free edition's 5,000 credits/day is tight for testing. 'Webhooks' covers the Notification API (watch data changes) plus workflow webhooks.

one_liner: Sales CRM with built-in calling, email, SMS and sequences for SMB teams.
auth_notes: API keys (Settings > Developer > API Keys) are tied to a user and org and sent via HTTP Basic (key as username, blank password); best for internal scripts. OAuth 2.0 apps for user-facing integrations: self-serve 'Creating an OAuth App', optional publish to the Integrations Directory.
access_notes: No free plan. 14-day free trial without a credit card. REST API on all plans per pricing FAQ, but 'High-volume API access' (with event log) is not on Solo. Plans: Solo $9-19, Essentials $35-49, Growth $99-109, Scale $139-149 per user/month. MCP server included on every plan.
api_breadth_notes: About 300 endpoint pages: leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, many activity types, custom objects/fields, sequences, bulk actions, smart views, reporting, webhooks/events, users/roles, phone numbers, templates.
mcp_notes: Hosted at https://mcp.close.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no SSE). OAuth 2.0 with Dynamic Client Registration, or API key via Close-API-Key and Close-Scope headers. Scopes: mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive.
blocker: No free plan; testing beyond 14-day trial needs paid plan
notes: Base URL https://api.close.com/api/v1. Webhooks plus a 30-day event log. OAuth app creation is self-serve; listing in the Integrations Directory goes through a publish step. Exactly what Solo's basic API access includes is unclear on the pricing page.

one_liner: CRM built for Google Workspace, tracking leads, people, companies and opportunities.
auth_notes: API key plus the generating user's email in request headers (legacy X-PW-* style). Only Admin users can generate keys (Settings > Integrations > API Keys). OAuth 2.0 (auth-code, Bearer) is 'preferred for partner integrations' but not self-serve: register by contacting Copper (partners@copper.com) with app name, purpose and HTTPS callback. Only scope is developer/v1/all.
access_notes: No permanent free plan. Pricing says 'Start free, no credit card required' (trial length not stated). Plans: Basic $23-29, Professional $59-69, Business $99-134 per seat/month. Which plans include the API is not stated; 'Integrations' is listed only on Professional and Business.
api_breadth_notes: About 14 resource groups: account/users, leads, people, companies, opportunities (pipelines, loss reasons), projects, tags, tasks, activities, custom fields, field layouts, related items, file upload, webhooks.
mcp_notes: No vendor MCP server found. Only third-party servers exist (Apideck, StackOne, Activepieces, Zapier, Composio, community GitHub projects).
blocker: OAuth needs manual Copper registration; API keys admin-only, no free plan
notes: Base URL https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1. A toolkit can ship today with admin API key + email auth (https://developer.copper.com/introduction/authentication.html, https://support.copper.com/en/articles/8823347-generating-an-api-key). OAuth needs Copper to issue client credentials. Plan gating of the API is unverified; confirm the trial includes API keys.

one_liner: Intapp's deal and relationship management platform for capital markets firms.
auth_notes: The user enables an API key in their profile (requires an admin to grant the 'API' site-area capability to their user group). Client ID + API key are exchanged via OAuth2 client_credentials at {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token for a 15-minute Bearer token. Scopes: data, user_management, publish, ri_import, backup. MCP uses an interactive per-user OAuth login with .well-known discovery (no client ID/secret).
access_notes: API keys exist only inside an existing DealCloud site, enabled by that site's admin or the DealCloud Customer Success Manager. No public signup, free tier or trial found; DealCloud is an enterprise Intapp product. MCP additionally needs a 'DealCloud with Celeste' license.
api_breadth_notes: Schema (entry types, fields, metadata), Data (cells, rows, history, files, merge, reports), User Management, Publications (event feed), Site Backups, Relationship Intelligence, Schema Contracts; roughly 20-100 operations.
mcp_notes: Intapp-documented DealCloud MCP server at https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud (site-specific, copied from Tools > MCP Servers). Per-user OAuth. Admin needs 'Manage MCP Servers'; users need the 'Celeste Member' group with MCP Access; write tools must be toggled on. Requires a 'DealCloud with Celeste' license. GA/beta status not stated.
blocker: Enterprise-only; needs Intapp customer site or partnership to test
notes: Public docs are good enough to build against, but testing needs a live DealCloud tenant. Base URL is per-site, so take it as a connection field. Real-time changes come through 'Publications' (a polled event feed with acknowledgements) rather than push webhooks. SDKs exist for Python and C#. 'partner_gated' rests on no public signup being found, not on an explicit vendor statement. Verdict could be 'blocked' if no customer or Intapp partner can provide a test site.
